stem:
Volunteers in the fictional town of Marlow Bay spent two summers rebuilding the harbor's old stone seawall by hand. The project was finished in ______ wall has since protected the docks from three major storms.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Split Test: 'The project was finished in 2019' and 'the wall has since protected the docks…' are both complete. Two complete sentences need a period, a semicolon, or comma + FANBOYS. Only the semicolon works. Trust the Split Test, not your ear.

distractor_notes.A: Comma splice: a comma alone can't join two complete sentences.
distractor_notes.B: Run-on: two complete sentences with nothing joining them.
distractor_notes.D: Fake joiner: 'however' is not a FANBOYS, so this is still a comma splice.

stem:
Botanist Leena Okafor, who studies desert plants, spent a decade tracking when cacti, agaves, and yuccas bloom across a stretch of the fictional Sorrel ______ data show that several species now flower nearly two weeks earlier than they did in the 1990s.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Don't let the inner commas scare you. They're harmless. Split it: 'Botanist Leena Okafor … spent a decade tracking…' is complete, and 'her data show…' is complete. Comma + FANBOYS ('and') is the only legal joiner here.

distractor_notes.B: Fake joiner: 'therefore' can't join sentences with a comma.
distractor_notes.C: Comma splice.
distractor_notes.D: Run-on: no punctuation between two complete sentences.

stem:
The architects of the fictional Orvieto Library expected readers to gather in its sunlit main ______ crowded into the small basement reading rooms, where the cool, quiet air made long study sessions easier.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Ignore 'however'. It's a fake joiner wherever it sits. Split Test: '…expected readers to gather in its sunlit main hall' is complete, and 'visitors crowded into the small basement reading rooms' is complete. You need a semicolon (or period) between them. Trust the Split Test, not your ear.

distractor_notes.A: Comma splice. Moving 'however' inside the second clause doesn't make it a joiner.
distractor_notes.B: Comma + fake joiner: still a comma splice.
distractor_notes.C: Run-on: nothing joins the two complete sentences.

stem:
The boto—a pink-skinned dolphin found in the rivers of South ______ uses echolocation to hunt fish in muddy water. Its clicks bounce off prey, letting it find a meal even when it can't see more than a few inches ahead.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Removal test: cut '—a pink-skinned dolphin found in the rivers of South America—' and you get 'The boto uses echolocation…'. Still a sentence, so it's extra info. It opened with a dash, so it closes with a dash. Same mark in, same mark out.

distractor_notes.A: Mismatched marks: the extra info opened with a dash, so it must close with a dash.
distractor_notes.C: No closing mark: the extra information never gets closed off.
distractor_notes.D: A semicolon can't close extra information.

stem:
Painter Mirela ______ who spent most of her career in a cramped studio on the fictional island of Gull Rock, did not hold her first gallery show until she was sixty. Every painting in that show sold within a week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: This time the blank is at the OPENING. Find the close first: the comma after 'Gull Rock'. Removal test: 'Painter Mirela Dunn did not hold her first gallery show until she was sixty' still works. So the pair is comma … comma.

distractor_notes.A: Mismatched marks: the extra info closes with a comma, so it must open with a comma.
distractor_notes.B: No opening mark: the extra information is never set off.
distractor_notes.C: A semicolon can't open extra information.

stem:
Engineers have long debated which bridge designs best survive earthquakes. In a recent set of simulations, researchers at the fictional Kestrel Institute found that ______ suffered far less damage than rigid bridges did.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choice_a: bridges, built on flexible rubber bearings,
choice_b: bridges built on flexible rubber bearings
choice_d: bridges, built on flexible rubber bearings
explanation: Removal test: cut 'built on flexible rubber bearings' and you get 'bridges suffered far less damage than rigid bridges did', which makes no sense. The phrase tells you WHICH bridges, so it's essential. Essential info gets no commas.

distractor_notes.A: Treats essential info as extra. Remove it and the sentence loses its meaning.
distractor_notes.C: Mismatched marks (dash/comma), and the info isn't extra anyway.
distractor_notes.D: A single comma splits the subject from its verb.

stem:
After months of planning, the fictional Fernwood Community Garden finally chose the three crops it will grow for the town food ______ squash, black beans, and collard greens. Volunteers will plant all three in early May.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Check the left side: '…chose the three crops it will grow for the town food bank' is a complete sentence. The right side is a list. Complete sentence + list = colon.

distractor_notes.A: A comma can't introduce a list after a complete sentence.
distractor_notes.B: A semicolon needs a complete sentence on BOTH sides, and a list isn't one.
distractor_notes.D: No punctuation: the list runs straight into the sentence.

stem:
The fictional coastal town of Port Elva banned plastic shopping bags in 2015 for one simple ______ the bags' habit of clogging the storm drains that kept downtown streets from flooding.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Left side: 'The … town … banned plastic shopping bags in 2015 for one simple reason' is complete. Right side: it explains WHAT the reason was, but it's not a full sentence. Complete sentence + explanation = colon.

distractor_notes.B: A semicolon needs a complete sentence after it, but 'the bags' habit of clogging…' isn't one.
distractor_notes.C: No punctuation: the explanation crashes into the sentence.
distractor_notes.D: A period leaves 'the bags' habit of clogging…' as a fragment.

stem:
Each summer, campers in the fictional Lake Tovey nature program learn to identify ______ loons, belted kingfishers, and great blue herons. By August, most campers can recognize at least twenty species by sight.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Trap alert: there IS a list, but read the left side. 'Campers … learn to identify birds such as' is not a complete sentence. No complete sentence means no colon. 'Such as' flows straight into the list with no punctuation.

distractor_notes.B: Colon after an incomplete clause: 'learn to identify birds such as' can't stand alone.
distractor_notes.C: A comma here cuts 'such as' off from its list.
distractor_notes.D: A semicolon needs complete sentences on both sides.

stem:
The collection of handwritten letters in the fictional Harwick County archive ______ more than two centuries of local history. Researchers visit every week to read the letters, many of which describe floods, harvests, and weddings.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Cross out the middle: 'The collection [of handwritten letters in the … archive] ___'. One collection, so singular: 'spans'. The present tense matches 'Researchers visit'.

distractor_notes.A: Matched the nearest noun ('letters') instead of the subject ('collection').
distractor_notes.B: Wrong tense: the passage describes the collection as it is now.
distractor_notes.D: An -ing form leaves the sentence with no main verb.

stem:
The number of students at the fictional Brightwater High School who choose to study a second foreign language ______ risen steadily over the past five years. School leaders credit a new exchange program with a sister school in Japan.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Cross out the middle: 'The number [of students … who choose to study a second foreign language] ___ risen'. 'THE number' is singular ('A number' would be plural), so 'has risen'.

distractor_notes.A: Matched 'students' or treated 'the number' like 'a number'. 'The number' is singular.
distractor_notes.C: An -ing form leaves the sentence with no main verb.
distractor_notes.D: Wrong tense: 'over the past five years' runs up to now, so it needs the present perfect.

stem:
The lead researcher, along with her two graduate assistants, ______ the fictional Pallas Glacier each spring to measure how far its edge has retreated. The team's records now cover eighteen years of change.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Cross out the middle. Anything between commas goes, and 'along with' never adds to the subject. That leaves 'The lead researcher ___', one person, so 'visits'.

distractor_notes.A: Treated 'along with her two graduate assistants' as part of the subject.
distractor_notes.B: An -ing form leaves the sentence with no main verb.
distractor_notes.C: Plural verb: matched 'assistants' instead of 'researcher'.

stem:
The fictional Calder Bicycle Company recently redesigned ______ most popular model, adding a lighter frame and wider tires for riders who travel on gravel roads.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: One company = it/its. The model belongs to the company, so 'its'. Check 'it's' by reading it as 'it is': 'redesigned it is most popular model' makes no sense.

distractor_notes.A: Used a plural pronoun for one company.
distractor_notes.C: 'It's' means 'it is', not possession.
distractor_notes.D: 'They're' means 'they are', and it's plural.

stem:
After months of debate, the city parks committee in the fictional town of Ridgeview finally approved a plan to restore the old botanical garden. ______ proposal calls for new greenhouses, repaired walkways, and free weekend tours.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Who owns the proposal? Go back one sentence: the committee. One committee = it/its, even though it has many members.

distractor_notes.A: Used a plural pronoun for one committee.
distractor_notes.B: 'It's' means 'it is', not possession.
distractor_notes.C: 'There' is a place word, not a possessive.

stem:
The fictional Brennan Museum lent three paintings to the Oakdale Gallery for a summer exhibition. When the exhibition closed, ______ returned the paintings along with a detailed report on their condition.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Two singular nouns came before the blank: the museum and the gallery. Any 'it' could point to either one. When a pronoun is ambiguous, the answer names the noun. The gallery borrowed the paintings, so the gallery returns them.

distractor_notes.B: Ambiguous: 'it' could mean the museum or the gallery.
distractor_notes.C: Plural pronoun for one institution, and it's still ambiguous.
distractor_notes.D: Reads as 'it has returned', which is still ambiguous.

stem:
In 1928, Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming ______ that a mold growing in one of his lab dishes had killed the bacteria around it. His observation led to penicillin, one of the first widely used antibiotics.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Clue word: 'In 1928'. A finished past date means simple past: 'noticed'.

distractor_notes.A: Random tense shift to the present.
distractor_notes.B: Present perfect can't be used with a finished past date like 1928.
distractor_notes.D: Future tense for an event in 1928.

stem:
Since the fictional Willow Creek Library began lending gardening tools in 2018, residents ______ more than 9,000 rakes, shovels, and pruners. The program is so popular that the library plans to double its tool collection.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Clue word: 'Since'. 'Since' means it started in the past and is still going, so present perfect: 'have borrowed'.

distractor_notes.A: Simple past ignores 'since'. The borrowing continues up to now.
distractor_notes.B: Future tense, but the 9,000 tools have already been borrowed.
distractor_notes.D: Simple present doesn't fit a total counted from 2018 up to now.

stem:
The fictional Hollis Theater opened in 1924 as a silent-film house. For its first few years, a live organist played along with every movie. Then sound films arrived, and the owners ______ the organ in a storage room. It sat there untouched for decades.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: No clue word in the sentence itself, so match the other verbs: opened, played, arrived, sat. They're all simple past, so 'stored'.

distractor_notes.B: Random shift to the present in a past-tense story.
distractor_notes.C: Present perfect for a finished past event.
distractor_notes.D: Future tense in a story that's already over.

stem:
The new octopus exhibit at the fictional Redfern Aquarium has an unusual feature: a lid sealed with heavy clamps. Because an octopus can squeeze through almost any gap larger than ______ hard beak, ordinary tank lids are not enough to keep one inside.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The beak belongs to the octopus, so you need possession. Its = belongs to it. It's = it is. Read it as 'it is' and it falls apart.

distractor_notes.A: 'It's' means 'it is': 'larger than it is hard beak' makes no sense.
distractor_notes.B: 'Its'' isn't a word. 'Its' never takes an apostrophe.
distractor_notes.C: Plural pronoun for one octopus.

stem:
Every spring, the fictional town of Linden Falls holds a baking contest at its farmers market. This year, the three ______ pies were all made with rhubarb grown on the same small farm just outside town.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Three finalists own the pies: many owners = -s'. 'Finalist's' is one owner, and 'finalists' with no apostrophe owns nothing.

distractor_notes.A: Singular possessive, but there are three finalists.
distractor_notes.C: Plain plural with no possession, but the pies belong to the finalists.
distractor_notes.D: Adds 's to a plural that already ends in s.

stem:
Ecologists have been studying the fictional Teller Marsh for more than twenty years. According to ______ rising water levels have pushed the marsh's egrets to build their nests higher in the reeds each year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Two decisions. 'Scientists' is plural ('ecologists … for more than twenty years') and owns the reports, so 'scientists''. 'Reports' just means more than one report and owns nothing, so no apostrophe.

distractor_notes.A: Singular 'scientist's' (there are several ecologists), plus an apostrophe on 'report', which owns nothing.
distractor_notes.B: No possessive: the reports belong to the scientists.
distractor_notes.C: Puts an apostrophe on 'report', but the report owns nothing.

stem:
Cities around the world are finding new uses for retired cargo containers, which often sit empty in ports for years. Built entirely from recycled shipping containers, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choice_a: forty vendors found space at the fictional Harbor Street Market when it opened last spring.
choice_b: the fictional Harbor Street Market opened last spring with space for forty vendors.
choice_c: the fictional Harbor Street Market's founders opened it last spring with space for forty vendors.
choice_d: last spring the fictional Harbor Street Market opened with space for forty vendors.
explanation: What was built from containers? The market. So the market has to come right after the comma.

distractor_notes.A: Puts 'vendors' after the comma, but the vendors weren't built from containers.
distractor_notes.C: Possessive trick: the noun after the comma is 'founders', not the market.
distractor_notes.D: The right noun is there but buried. 'Last spring' comes right after the comma.

stem:
Humpback whales sing long, complex songs, and males in the same region tend to sing nearly identical ones. After analyzing more than 500 hours of recordings made off the fictional Corran Islands, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choice_a: marine biologist Hana Ito's study found that the whales change their shared song slightly every year.
choice_b: the whales' shared song was found by marine biologist Hana Ito to change slightly every year.
choice_c: marine biologist Hana Ito found that the whales change their shared song slightly every year.
choice_d: it was clear to marine biologist Hana Ito that the whales change their shared song slightly every year.
explanation: Who analyzed 500 hours of recordings? A person: Hana Ito. Her name must come right after the comma, not her study and not the song.

distractor_notes.A: Possessive trick: the noun after the comma is 'study', and a study doesn't analyze recordings.
distractor_notes.B: Passive voice puts 'song' first, but the song didn't analyze anything.
distractor_notes.D: 'It' comes after the comma, and Ito is buried later.

stem:
Truffles grow underground, so farmers often depend on animals to find them. Trained for months to detect the scent of a rare truffle that grows beneath the forest floor of the fictional Varin Valley, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choice_a: Pip, a terrier owned by farmer Lucia Brandt, can now locate one from twenty yards away.
choice_b: farmer Lucia Brandt relies on her terrier, Pip, to locate one from twenty yards away.
choice_c: one can now be located from twenty yards away by Pip, a terrier owned by farmer Lucia Brandt.
choice_d: Lucia Brandt's training has made her terrier, Pip, able to locate one from twenty yards away.
explanation: Long opener, two possible actors. Who was trained to detect a scent? The dog. So Pip has to come right after the comma.

distractor_notes.B: Wrong actor: Brandt wasn't the one trained to detect the scent.
distractor_notes.C: Passive voice puts the truffle after the comma, but the truffle wasn't trained.
distractor_notes.D: Possessive trick: the noun after the comma is 'training'.

stem:
Most bats find food in the dark by echolocation, sending out high-pitched calls and listening for the echoes. ______ most fruit bats in the family Pteropodidae lack this ability and rely instead on keen eyesight and a strong sense of smell.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Cover, Connect, Choose. Sentence 1: most bats echolocate. Sentence 2: these bats DON'T. That's a contrast, so 'However'.

distractor_notes.B: Cause/effect, but echolocation in most bats doesn't cause fruit bats to lack it.
distractor_notes.C: Addition, but the second sentence goes against the first.
distractor_notes.D: Example, but fruit bats are an exception to the first sentence, not an example of it.

stem:
In 2016, the fictional town of Ashby removed an old dam from the Pell River, reopening forty miles of stream to migrating fish. ______ salmon returned to spawn in the upper river in 2019 for the first time in nearly a century.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Cover, Connect, Choose. Dam removed, river reopened → salmon came back. That's cause → effect, so 'As a result'.

distractor_notes.A: Contrast, but the salmon returning is exactly what you'd expect.
distractor_notes.B: Comparison, but sentence 2 is an outcome, not a similar case.
distractor_notes.D: Example, but sentence 2 is a result of sentence 1, not an example of it.

stem:
Many people assume that all sharks must keep swimming in order to breathe. Some species, such as the great white, do need constant motion to push water over their gills. ______ nurse sharks can rest motionless on the seafloor for hours, using muscles in their cheeks to pump water over their gills.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Connect to the sentence right before the blank: great whites MUST keep moving, and nurse sharks can sit still. That's a contrast, so 'By contrast'. Don't get distracted by the first sentence.

distractor_notes.A: Comparison, but nurse sharks do the opposite of great whites.
distractor_notes.C: Cause/effect, but great whites' needs don't cause nurse sharks' behavior.
distractor_notes.D: Addition, but this isn't another shark that needs constant motion.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Orla Pass Tunnel and the Brenn Valley Tunnel are railway tunnels in the fictional country of Vessaly.
• The Orla Pass Tunnel opened in 1911.
• The Orla Pass Tunnel is 6 miles long.
• The Brenn Valley Tunnel opened in 1987.
• The Brenn Valley Tunnel is 14 miles long.
• Both tunnels carry freight and passenger trains.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in length between the two tunnels. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choice_a: The Orla Pass Tunnel opened in 1911, while the Brenn Valley Tunnel opened in 1987.
choice_b: The Brenn Valley Tunnel, which opened in 1987, is 14 miles long.
choice_c: Both the Orla Pass Tunnel and the Brenn Valley Tunnel carry freight and passenger trains.
choice_d: At 14 miles, the Brenn Valley Tunnel is more than twice as long as the 6-mile Orla Pass Tunnel.
explanation: Read the goal first and make a checklist: (1) both tunnels, (2) a difference, (3) length. Only the correct choice checks all three boxes.

distractor_notes.A: A real difference, but the wrong attribute (date, not length).
distractor_notes.B: Mentions only one tunnel, so it can't show a difference.
distractor_notes.C: A similarity, but the goal asks for a difference.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Priya Varma is an ecologist in the fictional city of Halden.
• She counted the bird species living in 20 of Halden's city parks.
• Parks planted mostly with native plants had 31 bird species on average.
• Parks planted mostly with lawn grass had 12 bird species on average.
• Varma concluded that native plants support greater bird diversity than lawns do.

The student wants to present Varma's conclusion to an audience unfamiliar with her study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choice_a: Native plants support greater bird diversity than lawns do.
choice_b: After counting bird species in 20 Halden parks, ecologist Priya Varma concluded that native plants support greater bird diversity than lawns do.
choice_c: Ecologist Priya Varma counted the bird species in 20 of Halden's city parks.
choice_d: Halden parks planted mostly with lawn grass had only 12 bird species on average.
explanation: Checklist from the goal: (1) the conclusion, and (2) enough setup for someone who's never heard of the study (who did it and what they did). Only one choice has both.

distractor_notes.A: States the conclusion but never says who found it or how, which a new audience needs.
distractor_notes.C: Introduces the study but leaves out the conclusion.
distractor_notes.D: A true detail, but not the conclusion, and only one type of park.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The kora is a 21-string instrument from West Africa.
• The Celtic harp is an instrument from Ireland and Scotland.
• Both instruments are played by plucking the strings with the fingers.
• The kora's body is made from a large gourd covered with cowhide.
• The Celtic harp's body is usually carved from wood.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity in how the two instruments are played. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choice_a: While the kora's body is a gourd covered with cowhide, the Celtic harp's body is usually carved from wood.
choice_b: The kora is a 21-string instrument that is played by plucking the strings with the fingers.
choice_c: Both the kora and the Celtic harp have bodies made from natural materials.
choice_d: The kora, from West Africa, and the Celtic harp, from Ireland and Scotland, are both played by plucking the strings with the fingers.
explanation: Checklist: (1) both instruments, (2) a similarity, (3) how they're PLAYED. The 'natural materials' choice is the tough trap. It's a similarity, but it's about what they're made of.

distractor_notes.A: A difference, but the goal asks for a similarity.
distractor_notes.B: Right attribute, but only one instrument.
distractor_notes.C: A similarity, but the wrong attribute (what they're made of, not how they're played).

stem:
Many people assume that honeybees do nearly all the work of pollinating farm crops. However, a study led by the fictional ecologist Marta Selden found that on 40 farms, wild bees visited tomato and blueberry flowers more often than honeybees did, and fields with more wild bees produced more fruit. Selden argues that protecting wild bee habitat may matter as much as keeping honeybee hives.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choice_a: Wild bees may play a bigger role in pollinating crops than many people assume.
choice_b: Honeybees never pollinate tomato or blueberry flowers.
choice_c: Selden's study took place on 40 farms.
choice_d: Wild bees visit crops more often than honeybees, so farmers should stop keeping honeybee hives.
explanation: Predict first. 'Many people assume … However…' is the classic turn: people think honeybees do it all, but wild bees matter a lot. Match the prediction.

distractor_notes.B: Too extreme: the text says wild bees visited MORE often, not that honeybees never do.
distractor_notes.C: True, but it's a detail, not the main idea.
distractor_notes.D: Half right: the first part fits, but Selden never says to stop keeping hives.

stem:
For decades, art critics treated the quilts made by the fictional Ashgrove Sewing Circle as simple household objects. Recent exhibitions have challenged that view. Curator Dana Whitfield points out that the quilters planned bold geometric patterns in advance, arranging fabric colors to create visual rhythms much like those found in abstract paintings from the same era.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choice_a: The Ashgrove quilters were the first artists to use geometric patterns.
choice_b: Abstract painters of the era borrowed their designs from quilts.
choice_c: The Ashgrove quilts are carefully designed works that deserve to be seen as art.
choice_d: Dana Whitfield is a curator who has organized exhibitions.
explanation: Predict first: critics said 'household objects', and the new view says 'planned, artistic design'. The main idea is the new view.

distractor_notes.A: Too extreme: the text never claims they were the first.
distractor_notes.B: Off-topic: the text compares the two but never says painters copied quilts.
distractor_notes.D: True, but it doesn't answer what the text is mostly saying.

stem:
Some historians have suggested that the fictional port city of Varenna declined in the 1600s mainly because a rival port opened nearby. Records from the city's harbor office complicate this explanation. They show that shipping traffic had already begun to fall decades earlier, when silt from the river started making the harbor too shallow for larger ships. The rival port may have sped up Varenna's decline, but it probably did not start it.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choice_a: Varenna declined only because silt made its harbor too shallow.
choice_b: The rival port quickly became the busiest in the region.
choice_c: Harbor records suggest that Varenna's decline began before the rival port opened, likely because silt made the harbor too shallow.
choice_d: Harbor records show that Varenna's shipping traffic fell in the 1600s, proving that the rival port had no effect on the city.
explanation: Watch the hedges: 'complicate', 'may have', 'probably'. The text isn't saying the rival port played NO role, just that it didn't start the decline. Choices that say 'only' or 'no effect' are too extreme.

distractor_notes.A: Too extreme: the text says the rival port may have sped up the decline, so silt isn't the ONLY cause.
distractor_notes.B: Off-topic: the text never discusses how busy the rival port became.
distractor_notes.D: Half right: traffic did fall, but the text says the rival port 'may have sped up' the decline.
